scope: Corollary 13.3 (The logarithmic cutoff with 256 blocks) of the manuscript “From partial permutation information to Fourier bounds” (preprints/From-partial-permutation-information-to-Fourier-bounds-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 88926b5e48099ed8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 45. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n = 2d and suppose, for each sufficiently large integer d, that a probability w has an equal partition into q = 256 blocks with total complement entropy O(d4). There is v ≤ w of mass 1 − O(d−2) such that ∥b v(λ)∥2 HS ≤ 256C32ed6 D −1+34/256 λ . (13.8) In particular, whenever log Dλ > d8, this is at most D −1/2 λ for all sufficiently large d, uniformly in λ.
